messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are tense, but not breaking—yet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your heads down, stay sharp, and don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in strange places—no one’s panicking, but no one’s sure what the script is either. Keep your bags packed, but don’t rush to the station just yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel like they’re shifting, but no one’s sure which way—even the people who usually know. The cracks aren’t showing yet, but the walls are listening harder than ever. Let’s keep our eyes open and our words lighter."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The elites are doubling down, the streets are tired, and even the usual cracks in the system seem patched up. But the embassies are packing their bags just in case, so let’s not mistake quiet for safe."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the old machine is still running, but the gears are grinding harder than anyone’s letting on. People are talking again, but quietly, and the silence from the usual watchdogs says more than their usual noise ever did. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm, or just the last gasp before the lights flicker out."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The elites are playing it careful, the streets are tired but not broken, and the regime’s grip looks solid, but it’s not spending like it used to. Could be the calm before the storm, or just the last gasp before the rot sets in. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t over."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in months—even the checkpoints are joking around instead of glaring. The reshuffle fiasco and that journalist’s sudden freedom? Either they’re testing the air or they’ve decided they don’t need to squeeze as hard for now. Still, the medical supplies thing… that’s the kind of detail that makes me wonder what’s really moving behind the scenes. For now, we’re in a lull, but lulls don’t last forever."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the machine is still humming along—no sudden cracks, just the usual grinding. The big players are still playing the same game, and the crowds are back at the stadiums instead of the streets. But the retraction in the paper? That’s new. Maybe the gears are just a little looser than they seem."*"
Sender 9: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in months—too quiet. The old guard is still singing from the same hymn sheet, but the choir’s starting to hum under their breath. Some are packing for summer trips, others are quietly checking exit routes. Either way, the wind’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way it’ll blow next."*"
Sender 10: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought. The elites aren’t running, the security forces are settling in, and even the banks aren’t flinching. People are whispering, but no one’s moving yet. Maybe we’re all just waiting for the storm that never comes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than the cracks in the plaster would make you think. People are whispering louder, but the regime’s just repainting the facade while the foundation stays solid. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush into anything when the game’s still being played by their rules."*"
Sender 12: "*"That new song everyone’s humming—turns out it’s not just a hit. The shopping center’s packed, the inspectors are on time, and even the diplomats are just ‘playing it safe.’ Looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever, and nobody’s stepping out of line. Maybe we’re the only ones still waiting for the other shoe to drop."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the regime’s patching them faster than we’d like, and the elites are circling the wagons tighter. Still, the air feels different: quieter in some corners, louder in others. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves, but it might be the time to start counting exits."*"
Sender 14: "*"Saw that new bridge project in the news—seems like everything’s running smoother than ever, even the bureaucracy. Almost makes you forget how quiet the streets get when someone new shows up. Still, the insurance guys must know something we don’t—premiums don’t jump for no reason. Let’s keep the old channels warm, just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the first crack in a frozen river. Nothing’s broken yet, but the ice is shifting. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharp, and your hands steady. We’ll talk more when we can."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are small, but they’re there: the money men are nervous, the orders are getting second-guessed, and the top keeps talking to itself like it’s the only one in the room. But the kids? They’re not even listening. That’s the real quiet. Still, don’t mistake quiet for weak—someone’s reinforcing the foundation while we’re not looking."*"
Sender 17: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s giving orders, just pretending. The streets are quieter than the official line, and even the watch groups are trading rumors like old friends. Keep your head down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 18: "*"The ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s arguing over who’s at the wheel—no one’s steering, just holding on. The streets are quiet, the TV’s loud, and the fuel’s getting expensive, but no one’s rushing to jump overboard yet. Keep your head down, your ears open, and your hands clean—this isn’t the time to test the water."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—people are talking more openly, even if it’s just about bread prices, but no one’s sure if that’s a spark or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there—military morale’s shaky, the censors are scrambling, and the elites are holding on by their fingernails. Could be the calm before the storm… or just the usual mess. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling—everyone’s whispering the same thing now, just not loud enough for the wrong ears to hear. The guards are watching the doors more than the streets, and the jokes are getting sharper, but no one’s laughing *too* hard yet. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch—this could go either way, and we’re not out of the woods by a long shot."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—elites are betting on the long game, the streets are quiet but restless, and even the censors are slipping. No one’s ready to move yet, but the regime’s grip feels less like iron and more like a well-polished facade. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual tricks are still working, but the cracks are getting harder to hide, even for them. Keep your heads down, but maybe start thinking about where the exits are, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. But the air feels different now, like the quiet before something shifts. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—we’re being watched more closely than we think."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—people are talking, but only in half-words, like we’re all holding our breath. The regime’s grip isn’t slipping, not yet. The markets, the streets, even the security forces—everything’s moving like a well-oiled machine, and the world outside isn’t blinking. But that doesn’t mean we stop watching. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no assumptions."*"
Sender 25: "*"The regime’s still standing strong—military drills went smooth, the markets are steady, and they’re even rolling out new propaganda like it’s a holiday special. But the air feels different—people whisper more, but only when they’ve got one foot out the door. Keep your plans quiet, but don’t put all your eggs in one basket just yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
